notes.summary: This chapter covers West Bengal's geography (rivers, hills, forests and borders), its history from Plassey to the Bengal Renaissance and the freedom struggle, its culture (festivals, fairs, dances, crafts) and its state symbols. The Police Constable paper asks direct one-line questions such as 'which district', 'who founded' or 'which year', so knowing which district each famous place is in pays off most.
keyPoints: Borders: West Bengal touches three countries (Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan) and five states (Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Sikkim and Assam). It does not touch Meghalaya or Myanmar.
State symbols: animal – fishing cat; bird – white-throated kingfisher; flower – night-flowering jasmine (shiuli); tree – chatim (Alstonia scholaris).

Places and districts: Palashi (Battle of Plassey, 1757) – Nadia; Farakka Barrage and Hazarduari – Murshidabad; Bishnupur – Bankura; Santiniketan – Birbhum; Chhau dance – Purulia; Jaldapara National Park (one-horned rhino) – Alipurduar; Gangasagar Mela – Sagar Island, South 24 Parganas.

Rivers: the Bhagirathi-Hooghly flows past Kolkata. Farakka Barrage (1975) on the Ganga diverts water into the Hooghly to keep Kolkata port navigable. The Damodar was called the 'Sorrow of Bengal'. The Teesta, Torsa and Mahananda drain North Bengal.

History: the Partition of Bengal (1905) came under Lord Curzon and was annulled in 1911 under Lord Hardinge. The shift of British India's capital from Calcutta to Delhi was announced in 1911. Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society in Calcutta in 1784.

Reformers and institutions: Raja Ram Mohan Roy (Brahmo Samaj), Vidyasagar (widow remarriage), Swami Vivekananda (Ramakrishna Mission, 1897, headquarters Belur Math), Mother Teresa (Missionaries of Charity, 1950).

Heritage and GI: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway – UNESCO World Heritage Site (1999); Darjeeling tea – India's first GI-tagged product (2004); Sundarbans National Park – UNESCO site (1987); Durga Puja in Kolkata – UNESCO intangible heritage (2021).
Landmarks: Howrah Bridge (a cantilever bridge opened in 1943) was renamed Rabindra Setu in 1965. Vidyasagar Setu is a cable-stayed bridge. Victoria Memorial and Fort William are in Kolkata.
traps: Placing Palashi in Murshidabad. Siraj-ud-Daulah's capital was Murshidabad, but the battlefield of Plassey is in Nadia district.
Mixing up Curzon and Hardinge: Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905, and the partition was annulled under Hardinge in 1911.
Thinking West Bengal borders Meghalaya. WB's five neighbouring states are Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Sikkim and Assam.
Confusing Ramakrishna Paramahamsa with Swami Vivekananda. The disciple, Vivekananda, founded the Ramakrishna Mission and named it after his guru.
Calling the Royal Bengal Tiger the state animal. West Bengal's state animal is the fishing cat; the tiger is the national animal.
notes.examTip: Keep a one-page 'district → famous place' list for West Bengal and revise it daily, because many state-GK questions simply ask 'in which district is X?'.

questions.text: Who founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897, with its headquarters at Belur Math near Kolkata?
questions.explanation:
Swami Vivekananda founded the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897 and named it after his guru, Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
Its headquarters, Belur Math, stands on the west bank of the Hooghly in Howrah district.
Ramakrishna was the guru, not the founder, and Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Samaj.
Answer: Swami Vivekananda.

questions.text: The Gangasagar Mela, held every year on Makar Sankranti where the Ganga meets the Bay of Bengal, takes place on which island?
questions.explanation:
Gangasagar Mela is held on Sagar Island in South 24 Parganas district, at the mouth of the Hooghly.
Pilgrims take a holy dip at the confluence on Makar Sankranti (mid-January) and visit the Kapil Muni temple.
It is one of the largest fairs in India after the Kumbh Mela.
Answer: Sagar Island.

questions.text: Mother Teresa founded the Missionaries of Charity in 1950 in which city?
questions.explanation:
Mother Teresa started the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta (now Kolkata) in 1950 to serve the poorest of the poor.
Her home for the dying, Nirmal Hriday, is near the Kalighat temple.
She received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 and the Bharat Ratna in 1980.
Answer: Kolkata.

questions.text: The Howrah Bridge over the Hooghly was officially renamed in 1965 as:
questions.explanation:
Howrah Bridge, a cantilever bridge opened in 1943, was renamed Rabindra Setu in 1965 after Rabindranath Tagore.
Vidyasagar Setu (the second Hooghly bridge) is a cable-stayed bridge. Vivekananda Setu (Bally Bridge) is an older rail-cum-road bridge, and Nivedita Setu runs beside it.
Answer: Rabindra Setu.

questions.text: Palashi, the battlefield of the Battle of Plassey (1757), lies in which present-day district of West Bengal?
questions.explanation:
The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 between Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah and the East India Company under Robert Clive.
The battlefield, Palashi, is on the Bhagirathi in Nadia district.
Murshidabad was the Nawab's capital, which is why many students wrongly choose it.
Answer: Nadia.

questions.text: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 was carried out during the tenure of which Viceroy?
questions.explanation:
Lord Curzon announced the partition, and it came into effect on 16 October 1905, splitting Bengal into two provinces.
It triggered the Swadeshi and Boycott movement, and Rabindranath Tagore led Raksha Bandhan ceremonies as a symbol of unity.
The partition was annulled in 1911 under Lord Hardinge.
Answer: Lord Curzon.

questions.text: The Farakka Barrage, built across the Ganga to push water into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly and keep Kolkata Port navigable, is located in which district?
questions.explanation:
Farakka Barrage lies in Murshidabad district, close to the border with Malda district.
Commissioned in 1975, it diverts Ganga water through a feeder canal into the Bhagirathi-Hooghly to flush silt from the Kolkata port channel.
Answer: Murshidabad.

questions.text: Chhau, a vigorous masked dance based on martial movements, is a famous folk dance of which district of West Bengal?
questions.explanation:
Purulia Chhau is performed with large, colourful masks, often telling stories from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.
The masks are made mainly in Charida village of Purulia.
The other two styles of Chhau are Seraikella (Jharkhand) and Mayurbhanj (Odisha); together they were added to UNESCO's intangible heritage list in 2010.
Answer: Purulia.

questions.text: Jaldapara National Park in North Bengal is best known for protecting which animal?
questions.explanation:
Jaldapara, on the Torsa river in Alipurduar district, has the largest population of the Indian one-horned rhinoceros in West Bengal.
Gorumara National Park in Jalpaiguri district also has rhinos.
Red pandas live higher up in the Singalila and Neora Valley national parks, and Asiatic lions are found only in Gujarat.
Answer: One-horned rhinoceros.

questions.text: West Bengal shares its boundary with all of the following states EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
West Bengal's neighbouring states are Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, Sikkim and Assam.
Meghalaya does not touch West Bengal; parts of Assam and Bangladesh lie in between.
West Bengal also borders three countries: Bangladesh, Nepal and Bhutan.
Answer: Meghalaya.

questions.text: What is the state animal of West Bengal?
questions.explanation:
The fishing cat, a wild cat of wetlands and mangroves that catches fish with its paws, is West Bengal's state animal.
The Royal Bengal Tiger is India's national animal, which is why it is the usual wrong choice.
Other state symbols: bird – white-throated kingfisher, flower – shiuli (night-flowering jasmine), tree – chatim.
Answer: Fishing cat.

questions.text: Which product from West Bengal became the first in India to receive a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, in 2004?
questions.explanation:
Darjeeling tea was registered as India's first GI product in 2004 under the Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999.
The tag means that only tea grown and processed in the defined Darjeeling hill areas can be sold under that name.
Malda's Fazli mango, the Baluchari saree and Banglar Rasogolla received GI tags in later years.
Answer: Darjeeling tea.

questions.text: The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, popularly called the 'Toy Train', was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in which year?
questions.explanation:
The Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, a 2-foot narrow-gauge line climbing from the plains near Siliguri to Darjeeling, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1999.
The site was later extended as 'Mountain Railways of India' by adding the Nilgiri Mountain Railway (2005) and the Kalka-Shimla Railway (2008).
1987 is the year the Sundarbans National Park was inscribed.
Answer: 1999.

questions.text: The Asiatic Society, founded in Calcutta in 1784 to promote the study of Indian history and culture, was established by:
questions.explanation:
Sir William Jones, a judge of the Supreme Court at Calcutta, founded the Asiatic Society on 15 January 1784, with Governor-General Warren Hastings as its patron.
James Prinsep, a later secretary of the Society, deciphered the Brahmi script of Ashoka's inscriptions in 1837.
Answer: Sir William Jones.
